blog__ai-agent-cost-small-business.keywords: how much does an ai agent cost for a small business, ai agent cost, ai agent for small business, cost to build an ai agent, ai agent running costs, ai customer service agent cost, custom ai agent vs off the shelf, n8n ai agent cost

mainEntity.name: What is the cheapest way for a small business to try an AI agent?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switch on the AI agent inside a tool you already use, such as your helpdesk's website chat, and point it at your existing help content. Measure it for a month before paying for custom work. If it handles your common questions well, you may never need more.

mainEntity.name: Are AI model fees the biggest cost of running an agent?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not at small-business volumes. In our worked example of 3,000 conversations a month, model fees ranged from about $5 to about $216 a month depending on the model. The build and the upkeep tend to cost far more.

mainEntity.name: Can an AI agent take payments or issue refunds?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be connected to do both, but we don't recommend letting it act alone on money. Keep a person approving anything that moves money or commits you legally, and let the agent prepare the case so approval takes seconds.

mainEntity.name: Will an AI agent replace my staff?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most small businesses it takes repetitive questions and data entry off people's plates. Someone still has to handle exceptions, check its work and keep its knowledge current, so plan for changed roles rather than an empty desk.

mainEntity.name: Is customer data safe with an AI agent?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the provider's data terms and how the agent is built. Check where conversation data is stored, whether the provider uses it for training, how long logs are kept and who on your team can read them. Get those answers in writing before launch.

mainEntity.name: How quickly can a custom AI agent go live?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on integrations and how much the agent may do on its own. Arrowbin's published estimate is 2–3 weeks for a working prototype on your real data, then another 3–6 weeks to take it into production with integrations, security and monitoring.

mainEntity.name: Which AI model should a small business pick for an agent?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with the smallest model that passes your evaluation set, because it's the cheapest to run and usually the fastest. Move a specific step to a larger model only where the small one keeps failing, and recheck prices before you commit.

mainEntity.name: Do AI model prices go up or down over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both happen. Google's pricing page lists Gemini 3.6 Flash prices doubling on January 1, 2027, while Anthropic's page says Claude Sonnet 5 kept its $2 / $10 introductory price instead of rising as first scheduled. Date any price you rely on and check it again before signing a contract.

blog__chatgpt-shopping-for-online-stores.keywords: how to get products on chatgpt shopping, chatgpt shopping product feed, agentic commerce for small business, ai shopping agents ecommerce, agentic commerce protocol, universal commerce protocol, oai-searchbot robots.txt, product schema for ai search

mainEntity.name: Can I sell in ChatGPT without a Shopify store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Products from any platform can appear in ChatGPT shopping answers if OAI-SearchBot can read accurate, server-rendered product pages. A direct product feed needs approval through OpenAI's merchant program, and Shopify's Agentic plan is another route that lets you keep your current platform.

mainEntity.name: Does ChatGPT charge merchants to list products?

acceptedAnswer.text: OpenAI's commerce docs, as we read them, list no listing fee, and they treat ads as a separate program with its own requirements. Shopify says ChatGPT sales through Agentic Storefronts carry no transaction fees beyond standard processing rates. If OpenAI accepts you into its feed program, read the terms you're offered.

mainEntity.name: Should I block GPTBot to protect my product content?

acceptedAnswer.text: Blocking GPTBot is a content-licensing decision. It tells OpenAI not to use your content for model training, while ChatGPT search relies on a different crawler, OAI-SearchBot. You can block GPTBot and still appear in ChatGPT search, as long as OAI-SearchBot stays allowed.

mainEntity.name: If my product pages have structured data, do I still need a feed?

acceptedAnswer.text: You don't need a feed to be crawled, but a feed gives assistants fresher price and stock data. Third-party tracking published in September 2026 suggests feeds now supply most of the ChatGPT Shopping picks it follows. Keep the feed and the page saying exactly the same thing.

mainEntity.name: Why don't my products show up in AI shopping results?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually it's prices that only render in the browser, crawlers blocked by robots.txt or a CDN rule, missing or conflicting Product markup, and missing shipping or return details. For ChatGPT, not having a connected feed is increasingly a cause too. Check them in that order.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between ACP and UCP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are open protocols under Apache 2.0 for checkouts run by AI agents. ACP was developed by Stripe and OpenAI and is used in ChatGPT. UCP was launched by Google with retailers including Shopify and Walmart, powers checkout in AI Mode and Gemini, and Microsoft asks for UCP-ready feeds for Copilot Checkout.

mainEntity.name: Does any of this matter for stores in Bangladesh?

acceptedAnswer.text: The crawlability and product data steps apply in any market, because readable pages and open crawler access help everywhere. Checkout programs, though, are limited to certain markets, such as US buyers for Copilot Checkout and products eligible in the US, Canada or Australia for Google's UCP checkout. Check availability for your country before planning around them.

mainEntity.name: How long do robots.txt changes take to reach ChatGPT?

acceptedAnswer.text: OpenAI says it can take about 24 hours from a robots.txt update for its systems to adjust. If you also changed CDN or firewall rules, those apply straight away, so test with the crawler's user agent after both changes.

mainEntity.name: Do Steadfast, Pathao and RedX have APIs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. RedX publishes its API documentation openly, including a sandbox and webhooks. Steadfast offers API keys and an official WooCommerce plugin, and Pathao provides API access to merchants through its merchant panel, where the docs sit behind a login.

mainEntity.name: Is there a sandbox for testing a courier integration?

acceptedAnswer.text: RedX publishes a sandbox base URL, sandbox.redx.com.bd/v1.0.0-beta, where operations are simulated and don't touch real data. For Steadfast and Pathao, ask for test credentials before development starts. If there's no sandbox, agree a small test plan with the courier before you book real parcels.

mainEntity.name: Can I connect a courier to a Shopify store in Bangladesh?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. RedX lists an official Shopify app, RedX Delivery, which its App Store listing shows as free. For other couriers, search the Shopify App Store and check who publishes each app before you install it, because some are made by third parties.

mainEntity.name: Where do I get courier API credentials?

acceptedAnswer.text: From your merchant account with each courier. RedX's developer page has a token request option. Steadfast's plugin asks for an API key and a secret key, which its listing says come from your merchant dashboard or Steadfast support.

mainEntity.name: What does Steadfast charge for cash on delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Steadfast's pricing page lists a 1% cash on delivery and risk management charge. Delivery charges depend on route and weight, its pick and drop service has a ৳80 minimum, and charges exclude VAT and tax. mainEntity.name: Can one store use two couriers at the same time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A custom integration can route each parcel by area, price or courier health and still show your team one status view. Single-courier plugins handle one courier each, so running two through plugins means two places to check.

mainEntity.name: Do webhooks replace tracking checks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not fully. Use webhooks for speed, then confirm important changes such as delivered or paid through the courier's own API before you update the order. A daily polling sweep also catches parcels whose webhooks never arrived.

mainEntity.name: Why does the courier ask for the parcel's declared value?

acceptedAnswer.text: RedX's create-parcel call requires a value field, which its docs describe as the declared value of the parcel for compensation calculation. Declare what the goods are actually worth, and get each courier's compensation terms in writing before you rely on them.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between an MVP and a prototype?

acceptedAnswer.text: A prototype demonstrates an idea (often clickable mockups), while an MVP is a real, working product that users can actually use and pay for. The MVP is what you launch to learn from the market.

mainEntity.name: Should I build an MVP if I have funding for the full product?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually yes. An MVP tests your assumptions with real users before you invest heavily, which sharply cuts the risk of building the wrong thing. It also gets you to market months sooner.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to build an MVP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most well-scoped MVPs take 6–14 weeks from kickoff to launch. A simple single-workflow tool can ship in 6–8 weeks, while a complex multi-tenant SaaS MVP usually takes 14–20 weeks.

mainEntity.name: Can an MVP be built in 4 weeks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, for a very narrow, single-feature tool with a reused design system and no complex integrations. Most genuinely useful MVPs need at least 6–8 weeks to be stable and usable.

mainEntity.name: What's the most common reason MVPs take longer than planned?

acceptedAnswer.text: Scope creep. Adding 'just one more feature' during the build is the single biggest cause of slipped MVP timelines. Locking scope before development starts is the best protection.

mainEntity.name: How many features should an MVP have?

acceptedAnswer.text: As few as possible while still delivering your core value end to end. Often that means one primary workflow plus the minimum around it, such as sign-in and basic data. Everything else can wait for v2.

mainEntity.name: What happens after the MVP launches?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gather real usage data and feedback, then iterate. That usually means fixing the rough edges users hit first, leaning into whatever is clearly working, and adding the features people keep asking for. The MVP is the start of the product, not the end.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to build an MVP?

acceptedAnswer.text: A simple MVP typically costs $5,000 to $30,000, while a standard MVP with accounts, a database and a few integrations usually runs $30,000 to $90,000. The figure tracks scope, technical complexity and how senior your team is. Our custom software cost guide breaks the ranges down in detail.

mainEntity.name: Is custom software cheaper than off-the-shelf?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upfront, off-the-shelf is usually cheaper. Over time, custom software often wins. There are no per-seat fees, you don't pay for features you never use, and it fits your workflow exactly, which saves hours of manual work. In our experience, growing teams often reach the break-even point within 2–3 years.

mainEntity.name: Can I build custom software in phases to spread the cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and we strongly recommend it. Launch a focused MVP first, then expand in phases funded by the value (and revenue) the product creates. This lowers upfront risk and lets real user feedback guide where you spend next.

mainEntity.name: Why are two quotes for the same app so different?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually because of team seniority, location and what's included. A low quote may leave out discovery, design or QA, or lean on junior developers. Compare what each quote actually covers, not just the bottom-line number.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to maintain custom software?

acceptedAnswer.text: As a rule of thumb, plan for roughly 15–20% of the original build cost per year (an Arrowbin estimate). That covers hosting, third-party services, security patches, bug fixes and small improvements. It's the cost of keeping the product reliable and current.

mainEntity.name: Does location really change the price that much?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. By our 2026 estimate, senior team rates range from around $120–180/hour in North America to $25–60/hour in South Asia. The same product can cost three to five times more depending on where your team is based.

mainEntity.name: Should I get a fixed price or pay hourly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a fixed price for a well-defined MVP so you have budget certainty, then move to time & materials for ongoing development once the product is live and evolving. Running a short paid discovery first makes a fixed price far more accurate.

mainEntity.name: How accurate is an estimate before discovery?

acceptedAnswer.text: A pre-discovery estimate is a planning range, not a commitment. A short discovery phase covering requirements, user flows and architecture lets a team give you a tight, reliable fixed price, which is why we always recommend it before the main build.

mainEntity.name: Should I hire freelancers or an agency?

acceptedAnswer.text: Freelancers can be great for small, well-defined tasks. For anything ongoing or complex, an agency gives you a full team across design, engineering, QA and project management, plus continuity if one person is unavailable.

mainEntity.name: How important is location and time zone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Less than it used to be. What matters is overlap for real-time communication and clear, reliable processes. Arrowbin works with clients worldwide, across time zones.

mainEntity.name: What questions should I ask a software development company?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask to see and use their live work, who exactly will build your project and how senior they are, how they communicate progress, what their testing and security process is, whether you own the code, and what post-launch support looks like.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a development company is reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Reliability shows up as live, usable products, references who'd hire them again, a clear process for testing and communication, and honest, responsive behaviour during the sales conversation. Vagueness and slow replies are the warning signs.

mainEntity.name: Should I always choose the cheapest quote?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The cheapest quote often leaves out discovery, design or QA, or relies on junior developers, which leads to rework that costs more overall. Compare what's included and who's building it, then treat price as a tiebreaker.

mainEntity.name: Do I own the source code if an agency builds my software?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should. Confirm in writing that you own the source code, accounts and infrastructure outright. A trustworthy partner has no problem with this; reluctance here is a serious red flag.

mainEntity.name: Can I build an MVP for under $10,000?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes. A narrow single-workflow tool built on a reused design system with hosted login can land there, and so can a no-code or AI-built prototype. Expect one platform and few integrations. Be ready to rebuild parts of it if it takes off.

mainEntity.name: Is a very cheap MVP quote a red flag?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not on its own, but check what it leaves out. Divide the total by the number of weeks and ask how many people are on the team. Then check that discovery and QA show up as their own lines. A low quote with none of those usually means the cost turns up later as rework.

mainEntity.name: Should my MVP be a web app or a mobile app?

acceptedAnswer.text: Web first, in most cases. A responsive web app works on phones, ships from one codebase and skips app store review. Go mobile first only when the product depends on phone features such as the camera, location or push notifications.

mainEntity.name: What does it cost to put an MVP on the App Store and Google Play?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple's Developer Program is 99 USD per membership year, and prices can vary by region. Google Play charges a one-time US$25 registration fee. Those are only the account fees; the bigger cost of a mobile MVP is building and testing for each platform.

mainEntity.name: Are freelancers cheaper for building an MVP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often per hour, not always per project. With freelancers you become the project manager and the QA lead, and you're the one who joins design to code. If someone leaves mid-build, continuity is your problem too.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a technical co-founder before paying for an MVP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not to get it built. You do need someone who can make technical decisions after launch, read a quote critically and hold the code and accounts. That can be a co-founder, a fractional CTO or a development partner you trust.

mainEntity.name: How do I stop an MVP budget from growing during the build?

acceptedAnswer.text: Lock the feature list after discovery and keep a written list of what's out of scope. Put new ideas on a version-two list instead of into the current sprint, and ask for a price before you approve any change. Weekly demos help because you see drift early.

mainEntity.name: How much money should I keep back after the MVP launches?

acceptedAnswer.text: As a rule of thumb, roughly 15–20% of the build cost per year to run and maintain it (an Arrowbin estimate), plus a separate budget for the features users ask for. On a $60,000 build that's about $9,000–$12,000 a year before any new features.

mainEntity.name: Which is the best payment gateway in Bangladesh for an ecommerce website?

acceptedAnswer.text: There isn't one best gateway for every store. An aggregator such as SSLCommerz covers cards and the main mobile wallets with one integration, which suits most new stores. A direct bKash integration makes sense once bKash carries most of your online payments.

mainEntity.name: Can I accept bKash on my website without a payment gateway?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can ask customers to send money to a bKash number, but that isn't an integrated payment. Your store can't verify it, match it to an order or refund it automatically, so someone has to check every payment by hand. A merchant integration, direct or through an aggregator, does that work for you.

mainEntity.name: Does Shopify Payments work in Bangladesh?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Bangladesh isn't on Shopify Payments' supported-countries list, and Shopify says stores in unlisted countries need a third-party payment provider. SSLCOMMERZ has a free app on the Shopify App Store for this.

mainEntity.name: How much does SSLCommerz charge per transaction?

acceptedAnswer.text: SSLCommerz's pricing page lists 2.5% per successful transaction and 3.5% for AMEX, plus a Tk 25,500 Basic plan marked non-refundable, as of October 15, 2026. On a Tk 2,000 order, 2.5% is Tk 50. Check the page again before you sign, because fees change.

mainEntity.name: Can I test bKash or SSLCommerz payments before going live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes for SSLCommerz, which runs a public sandbox with test cards and OTPs that you can sign up for yourself. For bKash and Nagad, ask for test credentials during onboarding. Either way, test a success, a failure, a cancellation plus a timeout before you switch to live keys.

mainEntity.name: Why does a paid order sometimes show as unpaid?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually the shopper paid, then closed the tab or lost signal before the redirect back to your store. If only the redirect updates your orders, that payment never gets recorded. Listen for the gateway's server notification (IPN) and query the payment status of stuck orders.

mainEntity.name: Should a new Bangladeshi online store still offer cash on delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for most stores. Keep it next to your online options, confirm COD orders before dispatch, and give shoppers a reason to pay online, such as a small discount where margins allow.

mainEntity.name: Can I use SSLCommerz and a direct bKash integration together?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. SSLCommerz already includes bKash, so a separate direct bKash button is optional. Running both means two merchant accounts and two settlement reports to reconcile, so do it only when direct features such as saved wallets are worth the extra work.

mainEntity.name: Can I stop maintenance once the software is stable?

mainEntity.name: What happens if my Android app isn't updated for Google Play's requirements?

mainEntity.name: Is a maintenance retainer worth it for a small business?

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my Google rankings if I move to Next.js?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some movement is normal, and Google's own site-move guide says to expect temporary fluctuation. What protects rankings over time is a complete set of permanent redirects to the closest matching pages, kept for at least a year, plus canonical tags and internal links that point at the new URLs.

mainEntity.name: Can my team keep editing in WordPress after the move?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with a headless setup. Editors keep the WordPress admin and its revision history, and Next.js renders the public site. Preview and instant publishing need extra wiring through draft mode and on-demand revalidation, so budget time for them.

mainEntity.name: Should I use 301 or 308 redirects?

acceptedAnswer.text: Either is fine for Google, which treats a 308 as equivalent to a 301. Next.js sends a 308 when a redirect is marked permanent in next.config, and there's no reason to change it.

mainEntity.name: What should happen to old pages I'm deleting?

acceptedAnswer.text: If a close equivalent exists, redirect to it. If the page is gone on purpose and nothing replaces it, return 410 Gone. Don't point hundreds of dead URLs at the homepage, which Google's site-move guide specifically warns against.

mainEntity.name: Is Next.js faster than WordPress?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be, because pages can be pre-rendered and served from a CDN with little JavaScript. A badly built Next.js site can still be slow, so measure Core Web Vitals before and after the move instead of assuming.

mainEntity.name: Can a WooCommerce store move to Next.js?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can keep WooCommerce as the back end and build a Next.js storefront on its Store API, or move products and checkout to another system entirely. Plan order history and customer accounts before you pick a route.

mainEntity.name: Do I need Vercel to host a Next.js site?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Next.js runs on any Node.js server or in a Docker container with full feature support. Check your platform's limits, though: Vercel, for example, caps redirects defined in next.config at 1,024.

mainEntity.name: How many redirects can Next.js handle?

acceptedAnswer.text: The redirects list in next.config works well for a map known in advance, and one pattern rule can cover thousands of WordPress date-based post URLs. For more than about a thousand individual rows, the Next.js docs suggest a lookup in Proxy instead.

mainEntity.name: Which e-commerce platform is best for my business?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most stores, Shopify is the fastest way to launch. If you need full design control, a complex catalog or top-end performance, a headless storefront on Next.js usually wins. We'll point you to the right one once we understand your catalog and goals.

mainEntity.name: Can you migrate my existing store without losing SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We move your products, content and customers across, with 301 redirects and careful URL mapping so your search rankings hold.

mainEntity.name: Will my store be fast and mobile-friendly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We build mobile-first storefronts that pass Core Web Vitals, and that speed helps both your conversions and your Google rankings.

mainEntity.name: Can you add bKash, Nagad or cash on delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We integrate local gateways like bKash, Nagad, Rocket and SSLCommerz, plus cash on delivery with order confirmation, alongside Stripe, PayPal and card payments for international buyers.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to build an online store?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Shopify store typically launches in 3–6 weeks. A headless storefront takes around 8–12 weeks, and a fully custom platform 12 weeks or more. We can launch a focused first version sooner and add features after.

mainEntity.name: Will I be able to manage products and orders myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your team gets an easy admin for products, prices, stock, orders and content, and we train you on it before launch. No developer needed for day-to-day changes.

mainEntity.name: Do you maintain software you didn't originally build?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We start with a code and infrastructure audit to understand the system, then take over maintenance with a clear plan to stabilize it and move it forward.

mainEntity.name: How does your support pricing work?

acceptedAnswer.text: We work on monthly retainers sized to what you need, from essential security and uptime cover through to dedicated ongoing development. You get a predictable cost and a defined response SLA.

mainEntity.name: What's your response time for critical issues?

acceptedAnswer.text: Critical, production-down issues get our attention immediately under the SLA, with response and resolution targets agreed in your plan.

mainEntity.name: What's included in a maintenance plan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every plan covers monitoring, security and dependency updates, backups, bug fixes and a monthly health report. Higher plans add faster response targets, 24/7 cover for critical issues and more development hours for improvements and new features.

mainEntity.name: Can we use the hours for new features?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Hours not needed for upkeep go into improvements and new features from a shared list we agree with you, so maintenance also moves the product forward.

mainEntity.name: Is there a minimum contract length?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plans run month to month after a short onboarding period. You can change plan as your needs change, and if you ever leave, we hand over documentation and access cleanly.

mainEntity.name: What if our software is old or in bad shape?

acceptedAnswer.text: That's common, and it's where we help most. We start with an audit, fix the urgent risks first, then modernise step by step, so there's no need for a risky big-bang rewrite.

mainEntity.name: Should I build a native or cross-platform app?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most products, cross-platform (React Native or Flutter) gives you native-quality results from one codebase and saves 30–40% versus building each platform separately. We only push for fully native when an app is heavy on performance or hardware.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to build a mobile app?

acceptedAnswer.text: A polished MVP usually lands between $12,000 and $40,000, depending on the features and integrations. We give you a fixed estimate once the core feature set is defined.

mainEntity.name: Do you handle App Store and Google Play submission?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We handle the whole release: store listings, review compliance, builds and updates, so your app goes live without the usual headaches.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to build a mobile app?

acceptedAnswer.text: A focused MVP usually takes 10–16 weeks from kickoff to the stores: about 1–2 weeks defining scope, 2–3 weeks of design and 6–10 weeks of development and testing. Store review then takes anywhere from a day to a week.

mainEntity.name: Can the app work offline?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We cache the data people need most, queue their actions while they're offline, and sync everything when the connection returns, so the app stays usable on a poor network.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the app and the store accounts?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do. The source code, the App Store and Google Play developer accounts and all app data belong to you. We work inside your accounts, never ours.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to build a SaaS MVP?

acceptedAnswer.text: A focused SaaS MVP usually takes 8–14 weeks to launch. We build the core workflow that proves value first, then expand once you have paying users and their feedback to work from.

mainEntity.name: Can you take over an existing SaaS codebase?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We regularly audit, refactor and scale products other teams started. In most cases we can improve performance and reliability without a full rewrite.

mainEntity.name: Do you help with subscriptions and billing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We set up plans, trials, metered usage and the full Stripe billing lifecycle, including invoicing and dunning.

mainEntity.name: What goes into a SaaS MVP, and what should wait?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your core workflow, sign-up and login, and billing go in from day one, usually with a simple onboarding flow and an admin view. Teams and roles, public APIs, SSO, white-labelling and native apps can usually wait until paying customers ask for them.

mainEntity.name: Which tech stack do you use for SaaS products?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually Next.js and Node.js with PostgreSQL, Redis for caching and queues, Stripe for billing, and AWS or Vercel for hosting. It's a proven, well-supported stack that's easy to hire for later. If you already have a stack, we work with it.

mainEntity.name: Is the product secure and ready for bigger customers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We build in tenant isolation, role-based access, encryption, 2FA and audit logs, and add SSO when enterprise buyers need it. We also set up monitoring, alerts and daily backups so issues are caught early.

mainEntity.name: Do we own the code and the product?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You own 100% of the source code, accounts and infrastructure from day one. There's no lock-in, and we document everything so your own team can take over at any point.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between UI and UX design?

acceptedAnswer.text: UX (user experience) design is about how a product works: the flows, the structure, whether people can get things done. UI (user interface) design is about how it looks, from visual style to typography and components. We do both as one process rather than handing them off between teams.

mainEntity.name: Do you provide developer-ready design files?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You get organized Figma files with components, tokens and specs, plus a design system your developers can build from directly.

mainEntity.name: Can you redesign my existing product?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We start with a UX audit to find where users get stuck, then redesign against measurable goals like higher conversion and better retention.

mainEntity.name: How long does a UI/UX design project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A focused product or website usually takes 4–8 weeks from research to dev-ready designs. A UX audit of an existing product takes 1–2 weeks. Larger platforms with a full design system take longer, and we agree the timeline up front.

mainEntity.name: Do you design for accessibility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, always. We design to WCAG 2.2 AA: readable contrast, clear focus states, large enough tap targets, proper labels and error messages. It makes the product better for everyone, not only people using assistive tech.

mainEntity.name: Can your team also build what you design?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Designers and engineers work on the same team, so designs are made to be built and nothing gets lost in handoff. You can also take the Figma files and design system to your own developers.

mainEntity.name: What will we receive?

acceptedAnswer.text: User flows, wireframes, a clickable prototype, final screens for every state and breakpoint, and a design system with components and tokens in Figma. You own all of it.
